title: A sync conflict is answered on the dashboard, field by field
description: When the Sync button gets `conflicted`, show each record both sides changed with its fields, and per field the two values to pick from — nothing preselected (same rule as the MCP sync elicitation). Submitting calls the existing `resolve` route (packages/server/src/routes.ts:245, core resolveConflict), then syncs again to push. So nobody needs a terminal to finish a sync. Build it as its own component under apps/dashboard/src/sync/ with its test.

brief.approach:
Score 5: a form over a union with two arms, and the whole value is that nothing is preselected — a screen that defaults a side silently picks for the human, which is the one thing this must not do.

**What already exists.** The Sync button landed in `apps/dashboard/src/App.tsx` (node `upby`) and already renders the `conflicted` kind by naming the records. The server's `resolve` route is `packages/server/src/routes.ts:261`: it takes `{ branch?, record, choices }` where `choices` is a record of field name → `'ours' | 'theirs' | 'keep' | 'restore'`, and calls `resolveConflict`. `Conflict` (`packages/core/src/conflict.ts:35`) is a union: `{ kind: 'fields', path, id, fields: FieldConflict[] }` where each `FieldConflict` is `{ field, ours, theirs }`, and `{ kind: 'archived', path, id, by }`. Both arms have to be rendered; the archived one takes `keep` / `restore` and is the case a reviewer will find missing.

**The component.** New directory `apps/dashboard/src/sync/` beside `decisions/` and `review/`, its shaping in a sibling `data.ts` with its own test, exactly as `decisions/` is built. It is a stopping screen — an `Overlay`, the same as `DistributionScreen` — because choosing between two versions of three fields is not a glance.

Per record: the id, and then one row per field showing both values side by side with two controls, `ours` and `theirs`, **neither selected**. For an `archived` conflict, one row with `keep` and `restore`. Use radio inputs in a named group per field, not a toggle and not a select: a radio group with nothing checked is a form that cannot be submitted by accident, which is the property being bought here.

**Nothing preselected, and nothing submitted until every field is answered.** This is the same rule the MCP sync elicitation follows (`askFields` in `packages/mcp/src/ask.ts` — "Nothing is defaulted, so a form dismissed without answering is not an answer", ADR 0010). Disable the submit until `Object.keys(choices).length` equals the number of fields on that record, and say what is still unanswered rather than only greying the button.

**One record at a time**, the way the MCP tool does it — it loops the conflicts, one form each. Submitting calls `op('resolve', { record, choices })`, then moves to the next; when the last one is answered, call the sync again so the merge lands and the push goes out. That last sync is the point of the node: nobody needs a terminal to finish a sync. Handle its result with the same per-kind rendering `upby` already wrote — do not write a second one.

**If the user closes the screen partway**, say what that means and make it true: records already resolved stay resolved, the rest are untouched, and running sync again brings up what is left. That is what `resolveConflict` already does (it returns `recorded` with what is `left`, or `done`); read its return and render the two cases rather than assuming.

**Wire.** `apps/dashboard/src/wire.ts` already has `op<T>(name, body)`; the resolve route needs nothing new there beyond being called.

**Tests** in `apps/dashboard/src/sync/data.test.ts` for the shaping (both union arms produce rows; a field with identical values — if `conflictsOf` can produce one — is not a question) and a component test for the behaviour that matters: the submit is disabled until every field is answered; no radio is checked on first render; answering all fields and submitting sends one `resolve` with exactly those choices; resolving the last record triggers one more `sync`; and closing partway sends nothing further.

Nothing outside `apps/dashboard` changes: the route, `resolveConflict` and the core merge are already right and are not this node's to touch.

acceptance.proves: no option is checked on first render, the submit stays disabled until every field is answered, submitting sends exactly the choices made, and closing partway sends nothing further — the human picks every side and the screen never picks one for them
a conflicted sync opens the screen, resolving the last record runs one more sync so the merge lands and the push goes out, and the Sync button's own per-kind sentences still render

acceptance.run: git grep -q "op('resolve'\|op(\"resolve\"" -- apps/dashboard/src && test -z "$(git diff --name-only development -- packages/server packages/core)"
acceptance.proves: the screen goes through the resolve route that already exists — the server and core's merge were not touched

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'archived' -- apps/dashboard/src/sync && git grep -q 'restore' -- apps/dashboard/src/sync
acceptance.proves: both arms of the Conflict union are handled — the archived case, with keep and restore, is the one a field-by-field form silently drops
nothing is preselected in the markup itself, not merely in the submit guard — the same rule the MCP elicitation follows (ADR 0010)
only the dashboard changed: no core, no schema, no server route, no CLI, no MCP tool
the form compiles against the real Conflict union and the route's choices record
biome and secretlint are clean, including the accessibility rules on the radio groups
